items.review_rationale: Examined all transition arrows and their indices: the maps go from i to j when j≤i, and composition is tested when k≤j≤i. This is an inverse diagram over a preorder, not a direct system or a prerequisite of directedness.

references.phrase: indexed objects M_i and transition maps

references.disposition: Identity transitions and f_ik=f_jk∘f_ij are the defining compatibility conditions, without an assumed cofiltered indexing set.

items.review_rationale: Read the full partial-order criterion, specifically adding antisymmetry to reflexivity and transitivity of a preorder. A partial order is not assumed linear or well ordered.

references.context: Order theory: antisymmetry property, i≤j and j≤i imply i=j

references.disposition: This is the additional antisymmetry axiom; it does not assert total comparability.

items.review_rationale: Inspected both prerequisite relation properties: a binary relation on I that is reflexive and transitive; antisymmetry is neither included nor inferred.

references.context: Set theory: binary relation on I as a subset of I×I
Relation theory: every i is related to itself
Relation theory: if i relates to j and j to k then i relates to k

references.disposition: The underlying set is not required to have a discrete, ordered or finite topology.

items.review_rationale: Read all fraction, denominator and equivalence clauses of S-inverse-M, retaining the witness t∈S; the ring S-inverse-R supplies its module structure. The localization construction is not a field of fractions unless additional hypotheses hold.

references.context: Commutative algebra: multiplicative subset of a commutative ring, containing 1 and closed under multiplication
Module theory: equivalence relation for localization of an R-module along multiplicative set S

references.disposition: The displayed witness is essential to equality of localized module fractions and is not ordinary equality of numerator cross-products.

items.review_rationale: Read the entire ring-localization fraction construction including a possible zero divisor, the t witness, and the commutative-ring context. Does not conflate localization with forming a field or inverting arbitrary zero divisors.

references.context: Commutative algebra: multiplicatively closed subset of a commutative ring, containing 1

references.phrase: ring fractions modulo the stated equivalence
references.context: Commutative algebra: equivalence relation on numerator-denominator pairs in localization

references.disposition: The witness corrects naive cross multiplication when S includes zero divisors; it is the specified fraction equivalence.

items.review_rationale: Inspected the full graded Ω complex and universal extension of derivations; distinguished exterior powers from tensor powers, and degree p from homology degree. The differential is defined on wedge products, with Ω^0=B.

references.context: Multilinear algebra: pth exterior power of a module over B
Homological algebra: cochain complex with degree-raising differential satisfying d²=0

references.disposition: This Leibniz-compatible differential rule extends the universal derivation and is not a tensor product operation.

items.review_rationale: Read the short separable algebraic-element definition, distinguishing element-level separability via its minimal polynomial from separability of an entire field extension.

references.disposition: The base field for the minimal polynomial is the given F, not necessarily a field of definition enlarged to E.

items.review_rationale: Read the full separable algebraic-extension statement; it requires all elements to be separable algebraic elements and has an explicit algebraic-extension hypothesis. No finite degree or Galois normality is assumed.

references.disposition: The quantification includes every element without restricting to primitive generators, finite fields, or algebraic closures.
